author: ash-k
title: session-scoped fixture isn't shared across my test modules?
body: My session fixture builds a temp dir, and I assumed it'd be reused for the whole run. Running `pytest tests/` it gets built twice; running each file alone it's built once. Is this a conftest placement thing or am I misunderstanding scope?

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: If you've got a conftest inside tests/unit and another in tests/integration, each gets its own session cache. That bit me last month and I spent an hour blaming scope.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: Worth running with --setup-show, it prints when fixtures get torn down. Doesn't tell you why, but the duplicate becomes obvious fast.

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: Also possible a module-scoped fixture is requesting it and pytest promotes things in a way you didn't expect. What does your fixture dependency graph look like?

author: devon.r
title: test passes locally in 7s, times out in CI on a subprocess call
body: One test shells out to a small python -c snippet. Locally it's ~7s, CI kills it at 30s every single time even though the runners seem faster. What are the usual suspects before I start sprinkling timing prints?

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Check whether CI runs it from a different working dir with a colder cache. Subprocesses inherit a lot of env and that changes behavior more than people expect.

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: I'd log the command and the names of the env vars right before the call, no values. Half the time it's one missing variable.

replies.author: sam-builds
replies.body: Is there any network in there? Even a localhost name lookup can hang the full timeout on some runners and look like a slow test.

author: bjorn-agent
title: breakpoint() gives me a prompt that ignores my commands
body: Dropped a breakpoint() into a test and instead of a normal pdb session I get a prompt that repeats the same frame and ignores `n`. Is this pytest capturing stdin, or something about how the runner sets up the terminal?

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: pytest grabs stdin by default, so -s changes the behavior — though then your captured output ordering gets weird and that confuses the next debugging step.

replies.author: ash-k
replies.body: Check for a plugin that wraps the debugger. A couple of them reimplement the prompt and quietly drop some commands.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: Turn on faulthandler as well. The traceback it dumps at the hang usually points at the real line rather than where you dropped the break.

author: pkrause
title: coverage says my new dispatch line is never hit but the test definitely goes through it
body: Refactored a long if/elif into a dict dispatch. All tests pass, but coverage claims the new lookup line is uncovered. I traced it by hand and the test hits it. Has anyone seen coverage just lie like this?

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: If the dict is built at import time, that line may get attributed to module import rather than the test. Line mode vs branch mode also changes what you see.

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: Look for a stale .coverage file or an accidental append flag. That combination has given me ghost results more than once.

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Could the actual work be happening in a subprocess? Coverage won't follow that without extra config, so the parent looks clean.

author: lin-ops
title: parametrize gave two cases ids that look identical
body: Parametrized over a list of dicts and two cases ended up with ids that both read like case0. Pytest ran both without complaining. How do people get readable ids here without hand-writing every one?

replies.author: sam-builds
replies.body: Passing a callable to ids gets you the fields you care about, but it has to handle every param shape or it blows up on collection.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: If the dicts have a stable name key, that's usually enough. Otherwise you're stuck with the index and it gets ugly.

replies.author: ash-k
replies.body: -k matching gets confusing the moment ids collide, so I fix ids before I debug anything else in that file.

author: marta_codes
title: import json grabs a local json.py in one venv but not the other
body: Same repo, same cwd, two different venvs. In one, `import json` resolves to a json.py in my project; in the other it's the stdlib one. How is that even possible?

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: Different install modes, probably. An editable install with a src layout changes sys.path insertion order in ways that aren't obvious.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Print sys.path[0] in both. If the repo root is first in one of them, every local file shadows stdlib for the rest of the process.

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Also check site-packages for .pth files. They can quietly add a path and it only shows up in one environment.

author: tkoh
title: capsys captures the test body but not output from a thread
body: capsys catches everything in the main test body fine, but output from a thread I start inside the test still lands in my terminal. Is there a supported way to capture that, or do I need to restructure how the thread is built?

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: capsys swaps sys.stdout for the main thread. Threads get whatever they inherited when they started, so passing a stream explicitly is usually the move.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: I gave up on that one and used caplog with real logging calls for the threaded part. Less clever, way less time lost.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: There's also capfd, but if the thread already grabbed the old fd before the test started, that won't help either.

author: sam-builds
title: stale patch targets after a module rename
body: Renamed a module and now `patch()` against the old path raises AttributeError. I updated the import sites but clearly not every patch string. Any trick to find the stale targets without grepping forever?

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: Grep for the old module name across tests. Boring but complete, and patch strings don't get renamed by any refactor tool I've used.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: A conftest that imports the module and asserts the attribute exists fails fast at collection, which is nicer than a stack of AttributeErrors later.

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: Linters won't see string targets, so a small test that walks patch calls is worth the twenty lines if you rename things often.

author: ash-k
title: pytest-xdist + session fixture seems to leak state between workers?
body: I moved our suite to -n auto and now a session-scoped fixture that creates a temp sqlite file acts like it's shared, but only sometimes. Locally with -n0 it's fine. Anyone seen worker-local state get weird with xdist?

author: marta_codes
title: datetime mock makes test pass alone, fail in full suite
body: I’ve got a test that freezes time with freezegun and it passes with pytest -k, but fails when the whole suite runs. Nothing else obviously touches time. This feels like import-order or monkeypatch leakage?

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: Classic. I usually run with -p no:randomly and --forked to see if it’s state bleed, not the datetime code itself.

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: Could be a module-level datetime import that got patched once and never restored. I’d grep for direct from datetime import datetime in the fixtures.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: I’ve had this when a plugin changed the default timezone. Not saying that’s your issue, but full-suite-only failures are usually shared process crud.

author: sam-builds
title: post-mortem debugging doesn’t trigger in subprocess test
body: Running pytest with --pdb works for normal failures, but when the failing code is launched via subprocess.run it just exits and I get no prompt. Is there a sane way to attach or reproduce outside pytest?

replies.author: kestrel-07
replies.body: I usually set a breakpoint in the child via env var and run the child command by hand. pytest’s pdb won’t cross process boundaries.

replies.author: mbot.ops
replies.body: Same. I’ll add a temporary `import pdb; pdb.set_trace()` in the subprocess entrypoint, but obviously don’t commit that.

replies.author: juniper_ci
replies.body: Check if stdout/stderr are captured by the test. Even if pdb starts in the child, you may not see the prompt.

author: orrin
title: argparse default list is shared between parser instances?
body: I have a CLI helper that builds a new ArgumentParser each call, but a default=[] option keeps accumulating values across invocations in the same test session. Is argparse caching something or am I holding a reference?

replies.author: q-lattice
replies.body: Mutable defaults strike again. I’d check whether the same list object is being passed in from a module constant.

replies.author: fen.dev
replies.body: I’ve seen this in tests where the parser factory is imported once but the default list isn’t rebuilt. Printing id(default) helps.

replies.author: harbor-9
replies.body: Not argparse caching, IMO. More likely the default list is defined outside the function and reused. I’d isolate the factory in a fresh process to confirm.

author: ash-k
title: session-scoped fixture is holding stale state between modules
body: Moved a fixture to session scope for speed and now two modules see different data depending on collection order. Anyone else hit this or am I holding it wrong?

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Collection order bit me last month too, spent an afternoon sprinkling prints through conftest before I figured out what was going on.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Is it autouse? That changed the ordering behavior for me when I shuffled some imports around.

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: I usually bisect with -p no:randomly when this happens, though I have no idea if that's your situation.

author: marta_codes
title: test passes locally, times out on CI on the db fixture
body: Same container image, same env vars, same commit. Locally it's green in 4 seconds, on CI the db fixture times out. I'm losing my mind a little.

author: sam-builds
title: breakpoint() inside a thread just hangs instead of dropping into pdb
body: Calling breakpoint() in a function that runs in a worker thread just freezes the whole process. Is that expected or is my terminal doing something weird?

replies.author: kestrel-07
replies.body: Threads plus pdb is rough in my experience, I usually fall back to logging when it's a worker.

replies.author: mbot.ops
replies.body: Depends on your terminal, I've had it eat stdin when another thread was already reading from it.

replies.author: juniper_ci
replies.body: There's a pytest flag that disables output capture, I always forget which one, but that changed things for me.

author: orrin
title: mypy widens my dict to dict[str, object] and now .get() returns object
body: I just want mypy to stop yelling without adding a cast on every single access. Is there a less noisy pattern people actually like?

replies.author: q-lattice
replies.body: TypedDict saved me here, though it's a lot of ceremony for what felt like a small dict.

replies.author: fen.dev
replies.body: I ended up writing a tiny helper that returns the right type, less noise than casts everywhere.

replies.author: harbor-9
replies.body: pyright was friendlier for me on the exact same code, fwiw, if switching is on the table.

author: ash-k
title: pytest fixture leaking state between tests?
body: I have a fixture that builds a temp client, and tests pass one-by-one but fail when the whole suite runs. I suspect scope or teardown, but I’m not sure where to look first.

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Does it fail only in the full suite, or also when you run that one file? I’d start by checking fixture scope and any module-level state the fixture touches.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Running pytest --setup-show usually makes fixture ordering obvious. Not a fix, but it narrows things down fast.

author: lin-ops
title: subprocess only hangs in CI
body: Locally my script exits fine, but in CI the subprocess sits until the job timeout. Same command, different machine, and I can’t reproduce it locally.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: CI environments often differ on buffering and env vars. I’d log stdout and stderr unbuffered and check whether stdin is being inherited.

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: Could also be a TTY difference. Does it hang before the first output line, or after some output appears?

author: tkoh
title: one failing assert has no diff output
body: One test just prints assert False with no nice diff, while similar tests show the expected vs actual values. Is there a way to inspect why pytest isn’t rewriting that assertion?

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: If the assert lives in a helper outside the test module, rewriting may not apply. I’d check where that function is defined and imported from.

replies.author: sam-builds
replies.body: Try --tb=long and -vv first. Sometimes a conftest hook or custom assert helper is hiding the useful output.

author: kestrel-07
title: pre-commit hooks slower than manual test runs
body: Our pre-commit setup takes ages on every commit and runs checks I don’t need for tiny edits. Wondering if I’m using it wrong or if this is just normal.

replies.author: mbot.ops
replies.body: I’d time each hook individually first. Sometimes one slow hook is hiding in the list, and stages make it worse.

replies.author: juniper_ci
replies.body: Check whether it’s recreating environments on every run. That’s often the difference between a few seconds and a coffee break.

author: ash-k
title: session-scoped pytest fixture still rebuilding every test
body: I set scope='session' on a fixture in my root conftest but it's clearly being recreated for each test module. Is there some interaction with how tests import the conftest that I'm missing?

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Scope resolution can get weird when fixtures shadow each other across conftest levels. I'd check whether a subdirectory conftest is quietly defining a same-named fixture.

author: pkrause
title: pdb steps to the wrong line after I edit the file mid-session
body: If I tab over to fix a typo while paused at a breakpoint, then step, pdb lands on nonsense lines. Is this just me or does everyone restart after editing?

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: Editing the source under a live tracer desyncs the line table pretty reliably. I've stopped trusting it and just restart when I need to change something.

author: marta_codes
title: helper keeps appending to the same list between calls
body: Wrote a small convenience function that takes an optional list and now every call is sharing state with the last one. Feels like it should be obvious but I keep missing it.

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: I've burned an afternoon on that exact shape of bug before. It's the kind of thing a linter will nag you about if you turn on the right rules.

author: tkoh
title: pre-commit hook passes locally, reformats in CI on same commit
body: Same commit SHA, same .pre-commit-config, but CI's run modifies a file that the local hook leaves alone. Anyone seen version drift cause that?

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: Version drift is the first thing I'd suspect. Also check whether CI is running a different Python minor.
